newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO agree to set Hebron committee to work.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO agree to set Hebron committee to work.

text.p: Israel and the PLO on Sunday resumed peace negotiations and said they would set a committee to work on carrying out a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank city of Hebron.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiatiators met for almost three hours under U.S. mediation at a joint liaison office on the Israel-Gaza border for their first talks since a wave of violence killed 58 Arabs and 15 Jews.

"In tonight's meeting, both sides reiterated their commitment to the interim (peace) agreement and its implementation on the basis of reciprocity," chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters.

He and the head of the Israeli delegation, former general Dan Shomron, said both sides had agreed committees on Hebron redeployment and civilian, economic and security matters, would begin work but a venue had yet to be set.

"We intend to work at a fast pace so we can reach agreement in all these areas so we can continue...the peace process", Shomron said. "Of course the committees see a need for non-violence and reciprocity so we can continue the process."
It was not immediately clear when negotiators would meet again.
